topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's aims, learning outcomes, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Sustained proliferative signaling and growth signal autonomy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream signaling cascades drive cancer cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block of terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how an inability to complete terminal differentiation keeps cancer cells proliferative in both leukemias and carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of programmed cell death
topics.groupedBecause: It details how cancer cells resist apoptosis through p53 mutation and alterations in mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit through telomerase activation and bypass p53-mediated stress and senescence barriers.

topics.label: Reprogramming of cellular metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolic pathways to fulfill biosynthetic demands through aerobic glycolysis, oncometabolites, and epigenetic alteration.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the necessity, timing, and regulatory balance of blood vessel recruitment required for tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and detection of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: It explores the biological stages, physical and environmental constraints, and clinical tracking of cancer cells spreading to distant organs.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with reflections on recent literature, summarizes the collective hallmark framework, and transitions to practicals.
